a: cizle is a library of video prompts, image prompts and Claude Code skills. Each skill is a tested, scene-by-scene guide for one kind of video: a product launch, a feature tour, an FAQ, a Meta or TikTok ad. Each prompt shows the demo it made and credits the person who wrote it. Copy one, make it yours.
Yes. Everything is free to browse, read and copy while we launch. Make a free account to see the whole library. There is nothing to pay and no card to enter.

q: Why do I need to sign in?
a: Without an account you see a random sample of 24 video prompts. A free account (Google or email, a few seconds) opens search, filters, every prompt and every skill. It also lets you like and save prompts, and it is how we know the library is useful to real people.

A searchable collection of real prompts that people wrote for video, image and motion work: motion graphics, explainers, product videos, 3D scenes and more. Each card shows who made it, a preview, tags and a link to the original post.

q: Whose prompts are in the gallery, and can I use them?
a: The prompts belong to the people who wrote them. We collect them from public posts and community libraries, credit the creator on every card and link to the original. Use them to learn and as a starting point for your own work. Do not republish or resell them. The Sources page lists every person credited.

q: How do I get a prompt removed or corrected?
a: If you wrote a prompt and want it changed or taken down, email hello@cizle.dev with the link to the prompt on cizle. We remove it within two working days, no questions asked.

q: How do I use a skill?
a: Open a skill, press Copy prompt or run its install command. The command saves a SKILL.md into .claude/skills in your project. Connect the cizle MCP server to Claude Code once, then ask Claude to make the video for your link. The docs page walks through it in five steps.

q: How do I use cizle inside Claude?
a: Sign in, open the MCP page and copy the one command it shows. Run it once in your terminal. After that Claude can search the whole library from the chat, show you a table and open any prompt or skill. There is no API key or token to manage.

q: Do I need an API key or a paid AI plan?
a: The skills are plain markdown, so they work with any coding agent that reads them. Rendering with the cizle MCP server runs locally with no model call and no API key: your agent writes the storyboard, cizle turns it into an MP4. You need Claude Code (or a compatible agent) for the agent part.

q: Who owns the videos I make?
a: You do. Videos and images you create with a skill are yours to use commercially. The skills and prompts themselves remain the property of cizle and their authors.
